title: Adjoint mates on cartesian derived sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with inverse sequences of sheaves of commutative rings $B^C_1\leftarrow B^C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ and $B^D_1\leftarrow B^D_2\leftarrow\cdots$, respectively. For each $n\ge1$ let $\mathbf C_n\subset\mathbf D(B^C_n)$ and $\mathbf D_n\subset\mathbf D(B^D_n)$ be full stable enhanced subcategories, using the enhanced derived module categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Stable here means containing the zero object and closed under equivalences, shifts and mapping cones. Write $C_n,D_n$ for their ordinary homotopy categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $m\ge n\ge1$, suppose the coefficient extension functors $T^C_{m,n}:\mathbf C_m\to\mathbf C_n$ and $T^D_{m,n}:\mathbf D_m\to\mathbf D_n$ are derived scalar extensions, with their tensor-associativity coherences [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Use the coherent section categories and their strict realizations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A cartesian section has specified equivalences $T^C_{m,n}M_m\simeq M_n$, or $T^D_{m,n}N_m\simeq N_n$, with all transition coherences.

Let $F_n:\mathbf C_n\to\mathbf D_n$ be enhanced exact functors with specified coherent equivalences $q_{m,n}:T^D_{m,n}F_m\simeq F_nT^C_{m,n}$. Assume the functor $C_n\to D_n$ has an ordinary right adjoint $G_n:D_n\to C_n$, with specified unit $\eta_n$ and counit $\epsilon_n$. Define the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$b_{m,n}:T^C_{m,n}G_m\longrightarrow G_nT^D_{m,n}$$
as the $F_n\dashv G_n$ transpose of
$$F_nT^C_{m,n}G_m\xrightarrow{q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1}}T^D_{m,n}F_mG_m\xrightarrow{T^D_{m,n}\epsilon_m}T^D_{m,n}.$$
Assume that these mates are isomorphisms on every object of $D_m$. Then the $G_n$ admit enhanced right-adjoint realizations and the enhanced mates are equivalences. The $F_n$ and $G_n$ induce functors $F,G$ on cartesian sections, with the transition on $G(N)$ given by $b_{m,n,N_m}$ followed by $G_n(T^D_{m,n}N_m\simeq N_n)$. They form an adjunction with actual section units and counits realizing the specified finite units and counits. The construction is natural for coherent transformations of the $F_n$, including composition comparisons.

For cartesian sections $M,M'$ of $\mathbf C$ and $N,N'$ of $\mathbf D$, let $\mathcal H_C(M,M')$ and $\mathcal H_D(N,N')$ be the inverse systems of derived global mapping complexes, with transitions given by derived scalar extension and the cartesian identifications. The mapping-complex transposes give an equivalence
$$\mathcal H_D(FM,N)\simeq\mathcal H_C(M,GN)$$
of coherent inverse systems, and hence an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$ after strict realization. Its forward map is $h\mapsto G(h)\circ\eta_M$ and its inverse is $g\mapsto\epsilon_N\circ F(g)$ on mapping complexes. These formulas, the unit/counit triangle identities, and their compatibility with coefficient maps hold as coherent section maps before passing to the homotopy category or taking any inverse limit. If an evaluation or tensor-Hom transpose is formed from already enhanced tensor operations and these units and counits, it is likewise a section map with the stated evaluations. No functorial lifting of arbitrary transformations given only on the homotopy categories is asserted.

proof.text: Work with dg models of the enhanced categories in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], using the derived dg functor categories of [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] and allowing quasi-functors (functors after dg replacements), rather than demanding a strict dg right adjoint on the original complex model. For one level omit the subscript. For $Y\in\mathbf D$ form the right $\mathbf C$-module $P_Y(X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D}(FX,Y)$. Choose a representative $Z_Y$ of the object $G Y$ and a closed degree-zero representative $e_Y:FZ_Y\to Y$ of the specified ordinary counit. Composition with $e_Y$ after $F$ gives a module map $h_{Z_Y}\to P_Y$. For every integer $r$ its map on $H^r$ is the ordinary counit adjunction bijection applied to $X[-r]$: indeed $H^r\operatorname{Map}(X,Z_Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(X[-r],Z_Y)$, and enhanced exactness identifies $F(X[-r])$ with $FX[-r]$. Thus this is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism for every $X$. All shifts lie in $\mathbf C$ by stability. This uses the ordinary right-adjoint hypothesis on all objects, not only degree-zero maps between unshifted inputs.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text: The assignment $Y\mapsto P_Y$ is already an enhanced functor, with action given by postcomposition. Its values are quasi-representable by step 1. Apply [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] to factor it through $\mathbf C$ and obtain an enhanced functor $\widetilde G$ with a coherent module equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf C}(-,\widetilde GY)\simeq P_Y$. Its universal elements give an enhanced counit $e:F\widetilde G\to\mathrm{id}$. Evaluation at identities gives the unit and inverse transposition maps: $\Psi(g)=e_Y\circ F(g)$, $\Phi(h)=\widetilde G(h)\circ\eta_X$. More explicitly $\eta_X$ is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{FX}$ under the inverse module equivalence. The equalities $e_{FX}F\eta_X\simeq\mathrm{id}_{FX}$ and $\widetilde G(e_Y)\eta_{\widetilde GY}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\widetilde GY}$ follow by applying this equivalence and its inverse to the universal elements. They are coherent homotopies, including naturality, because the equivalence is an equivalence of enhanced module-valued functors. Applying the inverse equivalence on full transformation objects in [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] to these homotopies gives homotopies of the represented functors, including their higher boundaries. Under the ordinary adjunction the represented objects identify with the specified $G Y$ by the unique counit-preserving isomorphism; that isomorphism is natural since both sides represent the same ordinary Hom functor. The units then agree as well since both transpose $\mathrm{id}_{FX}$. We henceforth use $G_n$ for these enhanced realizations with these identifications.

proof.text:
Construct the enhanced mate by the actual composite
$$b_{m,n}=G_n(T^D_{m,n}\epsilon_m)\circ G_n(q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1})\circ\eta_{n,T^C_{m,n}G_m}.$$
Every factor is enhanced by step 2 or the hypotheses. Its $H^0$ is exactly [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] applied to the square in the statement, so equals the specified $b_{m,n}$. By hypothesis its component at every $Y$ is invertible in $H^0\mathbf C_n$. Choose a closed representative of its inverse: the two inverse equations in $H^0$ are boundaries, hence supply homotopies to the identities. Thus these components are enhanced equivalences; a transformation with equivalence components is an equivalence of enhanced functors. The latter assertion can also be checked after Yoneda: take inverse module equivalences and corestrict them using [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda]. No invertibility is inferred from invertibility of $q$ alone.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text:
Check the mate cocycle before forming sections. Write $S_{a,b}=T^C_{a,b}$ and $T_{a,b}=T^D_{a,b}$, suppressing the given associativity comparisons. For $k\ge m\ge n$, the transpose under $F_n\dashv G_n$ of
$$b_{m,n,T_{k,m}Y}\circ S_{m,n}(b_{k,m,Y})$$
is, by substituting the formula of step 3 and cancelling the adjacent unit/counit by the triangle homotopy,
$$F_nS_{m,n}S_{k,m}G_kY\xrightarrow{q_{m,n}^{-1}}T_{m,n}F_mS_{k,m}G_kY\xrightarrow{T_{m,n}q_{k,m}^{-1}}T_{m,n}T_{k,m}F_kG_kY\xrightarrow{T_{m,n}T_{k,m}\epsilon_k}T_{m,n}T_{k,m}Y.$$
The coherence of $q$ identifies this with the transpose defining $b_{k,n,Y}$. For identity indices the unital coherence identifies $S_{n,n},T_{n,n},q_{n,n}$ with identities, and the formula is $b_{n,n,Y}=G_n(\epsilon_{n,Y})\eta_{n,G_nY}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{G_nY}$, the second finite triangle homotopy. These calculations apply to the entire given coherent associativity diagrams: composition with the unit and counit defines maps on their complexes of transformations, and transposition is an equivalence there by step 2. Apply that equivalence to each higher coherence of $q$; its inverse supplies a compatible higher coherence for $b$. Uniqueness here is the contractible fiber of an equivalence of mapping spaces, as in [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda], rather than uniqueness of a degree-zero morphism. Therefore all index strings, not just triples, are coherent.

proof.text:
Write $u_{m,n}:S_{m,n}M_m\simeq M_n$ and $v_{m,n}:T_{m,n}N_m\simeq N_n$ for cartesian structures. Define
$$u^F_{m,n}=F_n(u_{m,n})\circ q_{m,n,M_m},\qquad v^G_{m,n}=G_n(v_{m,n})\circ b_{m,n,N_m}.$$
These have the required sources and targets. All factors are equivalences, so both resulting sections are cartesian. Naturality supplies the same construction on section morphisms and higher homotopies. The coherence of $q$, step 4, and the original coherences of $u,v$ supply their composition laws. This is the coherent section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; take its strict realization only after constructing these functors. No uniform boundedness, flatness of a quotient, or preservation of K-injectives by evaluation is required.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text:
For an input $X\in\mathbf C_m$ and $Y\in\mathbf D_m$, the two mate identities are
$$G_n(q_{m,n,X})\,b_{m,n,F_mX}\,S_{m,n}(\eta_{m,X})\simeq\eta_{n,S_{m,n}X},$$
$$\epsilon_{n,T_{m,n}Y}\,F_n(b_{m,n,Y})\,q_{m,n,G_mY}\simeq T_{m,n}(\epsilon_{m,Y}).$$
For the second identity, transposing the formula of step 3 cancels $F_n\eta_n$ with $\epsilon_nF_n$, leaving $T\epsilon_m\,q^{-1}$; compose with $q$. For the first, use naturality of $\eta_n$ and of $q$ to rewrite its left side as
$$G_n\!\left(q_{m,n,X}\circ T_{m,n}(\epsilon_{m,F_mX}\circ F_m\eta_{m,X})\circ q_{m,n,X}^{-1}\right)\,\eta_{n,S_{m,n}X},$$
which is the right side by the finite triangle homotopy. Composing these identities with $u_{m,n},v_{m,n}$ and using naturality proves that $(\eta_{n,M_n})_n$ and $(\epsilon_{n,N_n})_n$ are maps of the sections constructed in step 5. Apply the same transposition maps to higher index strings as in step 4, so the homotopies are compatible with all transition coherences. This explicitly constructs section units and counits; it does not attempt to lift unrelated transformations of ordinary homotopy categories.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text:
The transposes on coherent section morphisms are $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NF(g)$, since the factors are section maps by steps 5-6. The first composite reduces as
$$\epsilon_NF(G(h)\eta_M)\simeq h\,\epsilon_{FM}F\eta_M\simeq h,$$
and the second as
$$G(\epsilon_NF(g))\eta_M\simeq G\epsilon_N\,\eta_{GN}\,g\simeq g.$$
The first homotopies use naturality, the second the finite triangle homotopies constructed from the module equivalence in step 2. They are homotopies of section maps by step 6 and its higher compatibility. Thus these formulas are inverse on the full mapping objects of sections and give the claimed adjunction. This proves its triangle identities as actual coherent section identities, without inferring an identity of sections from equality of their evaluations.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text:
Apply the same formulas to the levelwise mapping complexes. To verify coefficient compatibility, write $h$ for the variable in the derived mapping complex $\operatorname{Map}(F_mX,Y)$. Interpret the following as identities of morphisms of derived complexes, with their coherent homotopies, using the enhanced functor maps of step 2; strict dg models can be chosen after the replacements in [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda]. After coefficient extension its source is identified using $q^{-1}_{m,n,X}$. Naturality of $b$ and the first identity of step 6 give
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{m,n,Y}\,S_{m,n}(G_m(h)\eta_{m,X})
&\simeq G_n(T_{m,n}h)\,b_{m,n,F_mX}\,S_{m,n}\eta_{m,X}\\
&\simeq G_n(T_{m,n}h\circ q^{-1}_{m,n,X})\,\eta_{n,S_{m,n}X}.
\end{aligned}$$
After the cartesian identifications this says exactly that $\Phi_m$ and $\Phi_n$ commute with the two transitions. All units and counits have degree zero, so the calculation respects differentials and introduces no extra graded signs. Step 4 supplies its higher index compatibilities. The inverse $\Psi$ is compatible too: compose the displayed coherent identity with the inverse module equivalences of step 2 (equivalently use the second identity of step 6). Thus $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are inverse equivalences of the whole coherent inverse systems $\mathcal H_D(FM,N)$ and $\mathcal H_C(M,GN)$, not merely isomorphisms on their cohomology groups.

proof.text: For strict realization of the mapping systems, apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to the one-object point site with the constant ring sequence $\mathbf Z$. Module sheaves on this site are abelian groups, so its strict semilinear sequences are precisely $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})$. Its enhanced localization of sequence complexes is equivalent to coherent sequences of complexes; this equivalence retains all evaluation functors and detects equivalences there. It sends the coherent mapping-system equivalence of step 8, together with its inverse and homotopies, to an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$. No inverse limit is used in this construction.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: enriched adjunction, coefficient transposes, units and counits; agent-supplied details for the general enhanced section assertion.

proof.text:
Finally take a coherent transformation $a_n:F_n\to F'_n$ compatible with their coefficient squares. Its adjoint transformation $G'_n\to G_n$ is the explicit composite
$$G'_n\xrightarrow{\eta_n}G_nF_nG'_n\xrightarrow{G_n(a_n)}G_nF'_nG'_n\xrightarrow{G_n(\epsilon'_n)}G_n.$$
Write this mate as $c_n:G'_n\to G_n$. Its defining counit identity is
$$\epsilon_{n,Y}F_n(c_{n,Y})\simeq\epsilon'_{n,Y}a_{n,G'_nY}.$$
For one coefficient transition abbreviate $S=T^C_{m,n}$ and $T=T^D_{m,n}$. The two maps $c_{n,TY}b'_{m,n,Y}$ and $b_{m,n,Y}S(c_{m,Y})$ from $SG'_mY$ to $G_nTY$ have transposes respectively
$$T(\epsilon'_{m,Y})(q'_{m,n,G'_mY})^{-1}a_{n,SG'_mY},\qquad T(\epsilon'_{m,Y}a_{m,G'_mY})(q_{m,n,G'_mY})^{-1}.$$
For the first formula use the counit identity, naturality of $a$ across $b'$, and the second identity of step 6 for $b'$. For the second use that identity for $b$, naturality of $q^{-1}$ across $c_m$, and the counit identity at $m$. The coefficient square $a_{n,SX}q_{m,n,X}=q'_{m,n,X}T(a_{m,X})$ identifies the displayed transposes. The equivalence of full transformation objects from step 2 therefore supplies their coherent equality, including its higher index compatibilities. For an identity $a$, its counit identity is that of $\mathrm{id}_G$, so its mate is the identity. For $a:F\to F'$ and $a':F'\to F''$, set $c=a^*$ and $c'=(a')^*$. Naturality and the two counit identities give
$$\epsilon_YF(c_Yc'_Y)\simeq\epsilon'_Ya_{G'Y}F(c'_Y)\simeq\epsilon'_YF'(c'_Y)a_{G''Y}\simeq\epsilon''_Ya'_{G''Y}a_{G''Y}.$$
This characterizes the mate of $a'a$ and proves $(a'a)^*\simeq a^*(a')^*$ on the full transformation objects. For a composite of left adjoints $L F$, use the right adjoint $G R$; its unit is $G\eta^L_F\circ\eta^F$ and its counit is $\epsilon^L\circ L\epsilon^F_R$. For a third coefficient diagram with transitions $U$ and $L_n\dashv R_n$, the composite comparison is $q^{LF}_{m,n}=L_n(q^F_{m,n})q^L_{m,n,F_m}$. Its right mate is
$$b^{GR}_{m,n}=G_n(b^R_{m,n})b^G_{m,n,R_m}.$$
Indeed its transpose under $L_nF_n\dashv G_nR_n$ is
$$T^E_{m,n}(\epsilon^L_m\circ L_m\epsilon^F_{m,R_m})\circ(q^{LF}_{m,n,G_mR_m})^{-1},\qquad T^E_{m,n}=U_{m,n}.$$
To obtain this expression, apply the counit identity of step 6 first to $b^G$, move $b^R$ across $\epsilon^F$ by naturality, and apply that identity to $b^R$; the remaining two inverse comparisons are the inverse of the displayed $q^{LF}$. This is exactly the defining transpose of the composite coefficient mate. The representing-module equivalence then gives its comparison with any separately chosen right adjoint. Applying the inverse equivalence of full transformation objects to the coherence homotopies for the input comparisons gives the corresponding higher homotopies for these mates; their boundaries agree because this inverse preserves composition. This includes composition comparisons. Tensor evaluation and tensor-Hom transposition formed from the already enhanced operations and these units/counits are compositions of coherent functors and transformations. The section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserves precisely these operations, so their section evaluations and transposes are the stated ones. This asserts naturality for enhanced input transformations only.
